propositions.text: The Appellant is a citizen of El Salvador appealing the RPD's denial of refugee protection.
The Appellant submits new evidence for the appeal and asks RAD to accept it under Section 110(4) IRPA.
The Appellant requests the Board's decision be set aside and the matter referred back to RPD for a new hearing by a different member including the issue of inclusion.
Alternatively, the Appellant requests an oral hearing under Section 110(6) IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant, an El Salvador citizen, appeals the RPD decision, submits new evidence, and requests a new hearing or oral hearing under IRPA sections 110(4) and 110(6).

propositions.text: Section 111(1)(c) of IRPA allows RAD to refer matter to RPD for re-determination by a different panel.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that under IRPA Section 111(1)(c), the RAD refers the matter to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel.

propositions.text: Appellant fears MS13 gang in El Salvador and USA, fled El Salvador in 2000 to USA with temporary protected status.
Appellant re-availed in 2008, left USA after learning gang was still after him, then came to Canada after threats.
Appellant crossed into Canada without reporting, later arrested on outstanding US warrant.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges fearing MS13 gang, fled El Salvador to USA, then Canada after threats, and was arrested on a US warrant.

propositions.text: RPD hearing on May 14, 2014 focused on possible exclusion under Article 1F(b) of the Refugee Convention.
Pre-hearing discussion involved counsel and panel about facts, exclusion, witness testimony, and law, some without appellant present.
Panel clarified no re-trial of conviction in XXXX would occur during hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker held a May 14, 2014 hearing focused on exclusion under Article 1F(b), with pre-hearing discussions and no re-trial of conviction.

propositions.text: Panel requested written submissions on whether to consider potential defenses if charged in Canada for equivalent act.
Panel and counsel agreed on submission dates and tentative plans for decision on exclusion issue.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker requested submissions on considering potential defenses and set dates and plans for exclusion decision.

propositions.text: Panel excluded claimant under Article 1F(b) on August 21, 2014.
RPD erred by denying opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses, and make final presentations.
RPD made findings without questioning witness.
Appellant denied legal right to put case forward.
RPD breached procedural fairness and legitimate expectations by denying right to testify.
RPD erred by referencing appellant's 'oral testimony' which appellant denies giving.
RPD misrepresented appellant and spouse's relationship and showed disapproval in decision.
RPD erred by failing to do separate analysis under Section 97 of IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker excluded the claimant under Article 1F(b); the applicant alleges multiple procedural and factual errors by the RPD.

propositions.text: Appellant requests RAD grant appeal and refer matter back to RPD with different panel or order no exclusion and new hearing on inclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant requests the RAD grant the appeal and order a new hearing or no exclusion.

propositions.text: Section 110(4) IRPA limits evidence on appeal to new or previously unavailable evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that under IRPA Section 110(4), only new or previously unavailable evidence may be presented on appeal.

propositions.text: Even if evidence meets Section 110(4), RAD may still refuse admission; appellant must submit detailed reasons for admissibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains that meeting Section 110(4) does not guarantee evidence admission; appellant must justify its relevance and admissibility.

propositions.text: In Raza, FCA held 'newness' depends on event or circumstance proved, not document creation date.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Raza that newness of evidence depends on the event it proves, not its creation date.

propositions.text: Two affidavits disclosed in appellant's record lack mention under RAD Rule 29 or in Memorandum.
RAD will consider these affidavits for admissibility under Section 110(4) IRPA to be fair.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes two affidavits lack procedural mention but will consider them for admissibility under IRPA Section 110(4).

propositions.text: First affidavit from appellant's counsel attests to hearing May 16, 2014 recording and panel's statements about testimony and decision.

paragraphs.summary: The first affidavit from appellant's counsel attests to hearing recording and panel's statements about testimony and decision.

propositions.text: First affidavit is not new; it reiterates official record and is not material; it will be disallowed.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the first affidavit not new and disallows it as it only reiterates the official record.

propositions.text: Second affidavit from another lawyer attests to conversations between counsel for appellant and Minister's counsel, hearsay only.

paragraphs.summary: The second affidavit attests to hearsay conversations between appellant's and Minister's counsel.

propositions.text: Second affidavit is new, relates to post-hearing conversations, allowed and considered despite hearsay nature.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows and considers the second affidavit as new evidence despite hearsay concerns.

propositions.text: Counsel made submissions on RAD's role in reviewing RPD decisions.
Federal Court decision in Huruglica guides RAD to conduct hybrid appeal with independent assessment, substituting decision if differing.
Huruglica states RAD can respect RPD credibility findings but is not limited to intervening only for palpable errors.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Huruglica decision requires RAD to conduct hybrid appeal with independent assessment, respecting but not bound by RPD findings.

propositions.text: RAD will independently assess RPD decision and decide if appellant should be excluded under Article 1F(b).

paragraphs.summary: The court states it will independently assess the RPD decision on exclusion under Article 1F(b).

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred by denying opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses, and make final presentations.
RPD was required to consider Minister's exclusion request before inclusion hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues RPD denied procedural rights; the court notes RPD had to consider exclusion before inclusion hearing.

propositions.text: Section 101(1) IRPA lists grounds making claim ineligible for RPD referral, including prior refugee protection, rejection, inadmissibility, etc.
Section 101(2) IRPA defines serious criminality for ineligibility based on convictions punishable by 10+ years imprisonment.

paragraphs.summary: The court states IRPA Section 101(1) and (2) define claim ineligibility grounds including serious criminality with 10+ year sentences.

propositions.text: Appellant pleaded guilty in XXXX court to Sexual Assault 4th Degree with elements: accused 20+, victim under 16, not spouse.
Appellant pled guilty based on these elements.

paragraphs.summary: The court states appellant pleaded guilty to Sexual Assault 4th Degree with specified elements in XXXX court.

propositions.text: The Appellant pleaded guilty to sexual intercourse with a person under 16 who was not his spouse while he was over 20.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant pleaded guilty to sexual intercourse with a person under 16 who was not his spouse while he was over 20.

propositions.text: The RAD must consider if the conviction would be treated differently in Canada.
In Canada, no charges would be laid as the victim was actually the Appellant's spouse.
The plea bargain acknowledges the victim was not the Appellant's spouse at the time of assault and conviction.
The RAD recognizes the Appellant disagrees with calling the female a victim.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD must consider if the conviction would be treated differently in Canada; the applicant argues no charges would be laid as the victim was his spouse; the respondent says the plea acknowledges the victim was not his spouse; the court notes the Appellant disagrees with calling her a victim.

propositions.text: The RPD breached natural justice by not allowing the Appellant to testify, have witnesses heard, or present evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the RPD breached natural justice by denying him the opportunity to testify, have witnesses heard, and present evidence.

propositions.text: The RAD has carefully considered the issue and the doctrine of legitimate expectations.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD has carefully considered the issue and the doctrine of legitimate expectations.

propositions.text: The only issue now is natural justice.
Jayasekara states evaluation of crime elements, prosecution mode, penalty, facts, and circumstances is required for exclusion clause interpretation.
Presumption of seriousness can be rebutted by these factors but not by extraneous factors like persecution risk.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the only issue is natural justice; Jayasekara requires evaluating crime elements and circumstances for exclusion; seriousness presumption can be rebutted by these but not extraneous factors.

propositions.text: The RPD must allow the Appellant and witnesses to testify for proper evaluation of the crime elements.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RPD must allow the Appellant and witnesses to testify for proper evaluation of the crime elements.

propositions.text: The RAD listened to the May 16, 2014 hearing recording.
The hearing lacked the Appellant's testimony and right to make final submissions on exclusion.
The Panel did not allow testimony and ended suggesting later submissions would be allowed.
A tentative hearing date was set but did not work for some parties.
Before rescheduling, the Panel decided exclusion and notified the Appellant without allowing him to speak.

paragraphs.summary: The court found the May 16, 2014 hearing lacked the Appellant's testimony and final submissions; the Panel ended suggesting later submissions but decided exclusion without allowing the Appellant to speak.

propositions.text: The Panel disallowed testimony despite the Appellant's request, which was an error.
Refusing testimony and arguments breached natural justice and invalidates the decision.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the Panel erred by disallowing testimony; the court finds this refusal breached natural justice and invalidates the decision.

propositions.text: The RPD breached natural justice by not allowing the Appellant to testify, have witnesses heard, or make final submissions.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD breached natural justice by denying the Appellant testimony, witnesses, and final submissions.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA Section 111(1)(c), the RAD refers the matter to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel.

paragraphs.summary: The court orders under IRPA Section 111(1)(c) that the RAD refers the matter to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel.
